content.user_title: Write App Changelogs from Git History
content.value_statement: Release notes often miss the app changes users care about. This skill reviews Git history, follows existing Fastlane style, and updates the latest changelog.
actual_capabilities: Fetches remote Git tags and identifies the latest tag matching v*.
Collects commit titles and descriptions between the latest version tag and HEAD.
Filters infrastructure, pipeline, build configuration, and internal documentation changes.
Selects two to five significant user-facing features, fixes, or performance improvements.
Matches recent Fastlane changelog style and updates the highest-numbered changelog file.
limitations: Requires a Git repository with accessible tags and an origin remote.
Assumes changelogs use the Fastlane Android en-US directory structure.
Updates the highest-numbered changelog file instead of creating a new file.
Output quality depends on clear commit messages and accurate project version metadata.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Mobile Release
use_cases.description: Create concise release notes from app commits since the latest version tag.

use_cases.title: Summarize Sprint Changes
use_cases.description: Separate user-facing improvements from repository maintenance before publishing a build.

use_cases.title: Standardize Store Notes
use_cases.description: Match new changelog text to the tone and format of recent Fastlane entries.

prompt_templates.title: Draft the Latest Changelog
prompt_templates.prompt: Review commits since the latest v* tag. Draft a concise changelog with the most important user-facing changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a release note draft

prompt_templates.title: Match Existing Release Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Read recent Fastlane en-US changelogs, review commits since the latest v* tag, and draft the next entry in the same style.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on User Impact
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze changed files and commit messages since the latest version tag. Exclude maintenance work and select two to five user-visible improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Update the Changelog
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify the current version name and code, compare recent changelog style, summarize meaningful app changes, and update the highest-numbered Fastlane changelog file.
prompt_templates.scenario: Complete an advanced release preparation workflow

output_examples.input: Recent commits add offline search, improve startup speed, and update CI dependencies.
output_examples.output:
Welcome to Janus 2.4.0 (240)
- Search saved content while offline.
- Open the app faster.

output_examples.input: Recent commits fix notification crashes, refactor build scripts, and revise contributor documentation.
output_examples.output:
Welcome to Janus 2.4.1 (241)
Fixed a crash that could occur when opening notifications.

output_examples.input: Recent commits improve account recovery, add database tests, and update workflow files.
output_examples.output:
Welcome to Janus 2.5.0 (250)
Improved account recovery with clearer guidance and more reliable completion.

best_practices: Review the selected commits and version details before publishing the changelog.
Keep entries concise and describe benefits in language users understand.
Confirm the destination file is the intended changelog for the current release.
anti_patterns: Do not include CI, documentation, or build maintenance without direct user impact.
Do not copy technical commit messages directly into store-facing release notes.
Do not overwrite a changelog until the version name, version code, and target file are verified.

faq.question: Which commits does the skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews commits after the latest tag matching v* through the current HEAD.

faq.question: How many changes does it include?
faq.answer: It selects two to five significant changes that affect application users.

faq.question: Does it include repository maintenance?
faq.answer: It excludes infrastructure, pipeline, internal documentation, and unrelated build configuration changes.

faq.question: Where does it write the changelog?
faq.answer: It updates the highest-numbered file in the Fastlane Android en-US changelog directory.

faq.question: Does it create a new changelog file?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow updates the existing highest-numbered changelog file.

faq.question: How does it match the project style?
faq.answer: It reads recent changelog entries and follows their language, tone, and formatting.
